lessons.title: At the train station
lessons.goal: I can use English at a train station.

newItems.definition: One part of a train where people sit.
newItems.example: We sit in the first carriage.

newItems.definition: The person on a train who checks tickets.
newItems.example: The conductor checks our tickets.

newItems.definition: A fast train that does not stop much.
newItems.example: We take the express train to Florence.

newItems.definition: A train where you can sleep at night.
newItems.example: There is a sleeper train at night.

newItems.definition: Go into a train to travel.
newItems.example: We get on the train at nine.

mainWord.definition: One part of a train where people sit.
mainWord.example: We sit in the first carriage.

lessons.mainWordForms: Carriage is a noun. A carriage is one part of a train where people sit. We sit in the first carriage.
lessons.expression: We get on the train at nine.
lessons.use: Use this when you go into a train to travel.
lessons.expressionTask: Sam and Anna are at the station. What time do they get on the train?
lessons.grammar: present simple for timetables: The train leaves at nine
context: Sam and Anna are at the train station in Rome.
We get on the train at nine. The train leaves at nine.
dialogue: Sam, which train do we take?
We take the express train to Florence. It leaves at nine.
Do we get on the train now?
Yes. We sit in the first carriage. The conductor checks our tickets.
Is there a sleeper train to Florence too?
Yes, but we take the express train. It is fast.
lessons.listening: On Monday morning, Sam and Anna are at the train station in Rome. They take the express train to Florence. The train leaves at nine. They get on the train at nine. The conductor checks their tickets. Sam says, 'The express train is fast.' Anna says, 'Is there a sleeper train too?' Sam says, 'Yes.'
lessons.question: Where do Sam and Anna take the train to?
lessons.reading: On Monday morning, Sam and Anna are at the train station in Rome. The city is big, and the station is full of people. They take the express train to Florence. The train leaves at nine. At nine, they get on the train. They sit in the first carriage. The conductor comes and checks their tickets. Sam says, 'The express train is fast. We will be in Florence at lunch time.' Anna says, 'Is there a sleeper train to Florence too?' Sam says, 'Yes, there is a sleeper train at night. But we take the express train today.' Anna is happy. She says, 'I like the train. The first carriage is clean and quiet.'
lessons.readingQ: Why does Sam like the express train?
lessons.readingA: It is fast, and they will be in Florence at lunch time.
lessons.speaking: Tell a friend about a trip by train. Which train do you take? What time does it leave?
lessons.speakingSample: I take the express train to Florence in the morning. The train leaves at nine. I get on the train at nine. I sit in the first carriage. The conductor checks my ticket. The train is fast. I like the train. There is a sleeper train at night too. But I take the express train in the morning.
lessons.writing: Write a short email to a friend about a trip by train. Say which train you take and what time it leaves.
lessons.writingSample: Dear Tom, I want to tell you about my trip. I take the express train to Florence in the morning. The train leaves at nine. I get on the train at nine. I sit in the first carriage. The conductor checks my ticket. The express train is fast. There is a sleeper train at night too. But I take the express train in the morning. I like the train. See you soon. Best, Sam
lessons.sound: Carriage has its strongest beat on CARR. In carriage, say CARR clearly at the start. In conductor, say DUCT clearly in the middle.
lessons.model: We sit in the first carriage.
lessons.wordTask: Which train do Sam and Anna take?
lessons.wordSample: They take the express train to Florence.

newItems.definition: The way you go from one place to another.

newItems.definition: A small bus that goes between two places.
newItems.example: A shuttle takes us to the hotel.

newItems.definition: A person who goes to work by train or bus every day.
newItems.example: A commuter takes the 8 a.m. train.

newItems.definition: A train that goes under a city.
newItems.example: Take the metro to the centre.

newItems.definition: Go somewhere on a bus.

mainWord.definition: The way you go from one place to another.
mainWord.example: The bus takes a new route.

lessons.mainWordForms: Route is a noun. A route is the way you go from one place to another. The bus takes a new route.
lessons.expression: I travel by bus to work.
lessons.use: Use this when you go to work by bus.
lessons.expressionTask: Sam and Anna travel in Rome. How do they go to the city?
lessons.grammar: How long does it take: How long does the bus take to the city
lessons.pattern: How long does the bus take to the city?
lessons.task: How long does the bus ___ to the city?
lessons.example: How long does the bus take to the city?
context: Sam and Anna travel by bus in Rome.
I travel by bus to work.
dialogue: Anna, how do we go to the city today?
We travel by bus. The bus takes a new route today.
How long does the bus take to the city?
About thirty minutes. Many commuters take this bus to work.
Is there a metro too?
Yes. And a shuttle takes us to the hotel. The metro is fast.
lessons.listening: On Tuesday, Sam and Anna travel by bus in Rome. The bus takes a new route to the city. Sam asks, 'How long does the bus take to the city?' Anna says, 'About thirty minutes.' Sam says, 'Is there a metro too?' Anna says, 'Yes. A shuttle takes us to the hotel.'
lessons.question: How long does the bus take to the city?
lessons.reading: On Tuesday, Sam and Anna travel by bus in Rome. They want to go to the city. The bus takes a new route today. Sam asks, 'How long does the bus take to the city?' Anna says, 'About thirty minutes. A commuter takes this bus to work every day.' Sam says, 'Is there a metro too?' Anna says, 'Yes, the metro is fast. And a shuttle takes us to the hotel in the evening.' Sam is happy. He says, 'I like to travel by bus. The bus is slow, but I can see the city.' Anna says, 'Good. We travel by bus today, and we take the metro tomorrow.' Sam is very happy today.
lessons.readingQ: Why does Sam like to travel by bus?
lessons.readingA: The bus is slow, but he can see the city.
lessons.speaking: Tell a friend how you go to work. Do you travel by bus or by metro?
lessons.speakingSample: I travel by bus to work every day. The bus takes a new route to the city. It takes about thirty minutes. Many commuters take this bus to work. There is a metro too. The metro is fast. A shuttle takes us to the hotel in the evening. I like to travel by bus. I can see the city.
lessons.writing: Write a short email to a friend about how you travel in the city. Say how long it takes.
lessons.writingSample: Dear Lisa, I want to tell you about my travel in Rome. I travel by bus to the city every day. The bus takes a new route. It takes about thirty minutes. Many commuters take this bus to work. There is a metro too. The metro is fast. A shuttle takes us to the hotel in the evening. I like to travel by bus. I can see the city. Best, Anna
lessons.sound: Route has one strong beat: ROUTE. In route, say ROUTE clearly. In shuttle, say SHUT clearly at the start.
lessons.model: The bus takes a new route.
lessons.wordTask: How do Sam and Anna go to the city?
lessons.wordSample: They travel by bus to the city.

newItems.definition: A car, bus or truck.
newItems.example: A bus is a big vehicle.

newItems.definition: A big road between towns.
newItems.example: We drive on the highway.

newItems.definition: A place where two roads meet.
newItems.example: Turn left at the junction.

newItems.definition: Not able to move because the road is full.
newItems.example: We are stuck in traffic.

newItems.definition: The fastest speed you can drive.
newItems.example: The speed limit is 50.

mainWord.example: A bus is a big vehicle.

lessons.mainWordForms: Vehicle is a noun. A vehicle is a car, bus or truck. A bus is a big vehicle.
lessons.use: Use this when the road is full and you cannot move.
lessons.expressionTask: Tom drives in Rome. What is the problem on the road?
lessons.grammar: have to for road rules: You have to stop at the red light
lessons.pattern: You have to stop at the red light.
lessons.task: You have to ___ at the red light.
lessons.example: You have to stop at the red light.
context: Tom drives a car in Rome.
dialogue: Tom, why are we so slow?
We are stuck in traffic. The road is full of vehicles.
What is the speed limit here?
Fifty. You have to drive slowly in the city.
Turn left at the junction?
Yes. Then we take the highway to the city.
lessons.listening: On Wednesday, Tom drives a car in Rome. The road is full of vehicles. Tom says, 'We are stuck in traffic.' Anna says, 'What is the speed limit here?' Tom says, 'Fifty. You have to drive slowly in the city.' Anna says, 'Turn left at the junction?' Tom says, 'Yes. Then we take the highway.'
lessons.question: What is the speed limit in the city?
lessons.reading: On Wednesday, Tom drives a car in Rome. The road is full of vehicles. The car moves very slowly. A bus is a big vehicle. Tom says, 'We are stuck in traffic.' Anna asks, 'What is the speed limit here?' Tom says, 'Fifty. You have to drive slowly in the city. You have to stop at the red light.' Anna says, 'Turn left at the junction?' Tom says, 'Yes. Then we take the highway to the city. The highway is fast.' Anna says, 'Good. I like to drive slowly and see the city.' Tom is happy. He says, 'We are stuck in traffic, but we have time. The city is good, and the road is not bad.'
lessons.readingQ: What does Tom say about the highway?
lessons.speaking: Tell a friend about driving in a city. What is the speed limit? What do you have to do?
lessons.speakingSample: I drive a car in the city. The road is full of vehicles. We are stuck in traffic. The speed limit is fifty. You have to drive slowly in the city. You have to stop at the red light. Turn left at the junction. Then we take the highway to the city. The highway is fast.
lessons.writing: Write a short email to a friend about driving in the city. Say what the speed limit is.
lessons.writingSample: Dear Tom, I want to tell you about driving in Rome. The road is full of vehicles. We are stuck in traffic. The speed limit is fifty. You have to drive slowly in the city. You have to stop at the red light. Turn left at the junction. Then we take the highway to the city. The highway is fast. I like to drive in the city. Best, Anna
lessons.sound: Vehicle has its strongest beat on VEE. In vehicle, say VEE clearly at the start. In highway, say HIGH clearly at the start.
lessons.model: A bus is a big vehicle.
lessons.wordTask: What is the speed limit in the city?

newItems.example: The plane moves on the runway.

newItems.definition: A very fast train.

newItems.definition: A ticket you can use for a long time.

newItems.definition: Be careful of the space between the train and the platform.

mainWord.definition: A big building at an airport.

lessons.mainWordForms: Terminal is a noun. A terminal is a big building at an airport. Meet me at terminal 2.
lessons.use: Use this to tell people to be careful at the station.
lessons.expressionTask: Sam takes a train to the airport. What does he hear at the station?
lessons.grammar: present perfect for travel experience: I have taken the high-speed train
lessons.pattern: I have taken the high-speed train.
lessons.example: I have taken the high-speed train.
context: Sam takes a high-speed train to the airport.
dialogue: Sam, how do you go to the airport?
I take a high-speed train. It is fast.
Do you have a season ticket?
Yes. I have taken the high-speed train many times.
What do you hear at the station?
'Mind the gap, please.' And I see the runway from the terminal.
lessons.listening: On Thursday, Sam takes a high-speed train to the airport. Anna asks, 'Do you have a season ticket?' Sam says, 'Yes. I have taken the high-speed train many times.' At the station, Sam hears, 'Mind the gap, please.' At the airport, Sam goes to terminal 2. He sees the runway from the terminal.
lessons.question: What does Sam hear at the station?
lessons.reading: On Thursday, Sam takes a high-speed train to the airport. The train is fast. Anna asks, 'Do you have a season ticket?' Sam says, 'Yes, I have a season ticket. I have taken the high-speed train many times this week. I like the train.' At the station, Sam hears, 'Mind the gap, please.' He is happy. At the airport, Sam goes to terminal 2. He sees the runway from the terminal. A plane moves on the runway. Sam likes the airport. The terminal is big and clean. Sam says, 'The high-speed train is the best way to the airport. I have taken it many times.' Anna says, 'Good. I will take it next week.'
lessons.readingQ: How does Sam go to the airport?
lessons.speaking: Tell a friend about a trip to the airport. How do you go? Have you taken the train before?
lessons.speakingSample: I take a high-speed train to the airport. I have a season ticket. I have taken the high-speed train many times. At the station, I hear, 'Mind the gap, please.' At the airport, I go to terminal 2. I see the runway from the terminal. The high-speed train is the best way to the airport.
lessons.writing: Write a short email to a friend about a trip to the airport. Say how you go.
lessons.writingSample: Dear Tom, I want to tell you about my trip to the airport. I take a high-speed train. I have a season ticket. I have taken the high-speed train many times this week. At the station, I hear, 'Mind the gap, please.' At the airport, I go to terminal 2. I see the runway from the terminal. The high-speed train is the best way to the airport. Best, Sam
lessons.sound: Terminal has its strongest beat on TERM. In terminal, say TERM clearly at the start. In runway, say RUN clearly at the start.

lessons.wordSample: He takes a high-speed train to the airport.

lessons.title: A taxi ride

newItems.definition: A road that goes over another road.
newItems.example: Drive over the flyover.

newItems.definition: A small bike with a motor and pedals.
newItems.example: A moped is good in the city.

newItems.definition: Call a taxi by raising your hand.
newItems.example: We hail a taxi in the street.

newItems.definition: A place where taxis wait.
newItems.example: Wait at the taxi rank.

newItems.definition: Take someone in your car to a place.
newItems.example: Sam gives Anna a lift to work.

mainWord.definition: A road that goes over another road.

lessons.mainWordForms: Flyover is a noun. A flyover is a road that goes over another road. Drive over the flyover.
lessons.expression: We hail a taxi in the street.
lessons.use: Use this when you call a taxi by raising your hand.
lessons.expressionTask: Sam and Anna need a taxi. Where do they wait?
lessons.grammar: will for offers: I will call a taxi for you
lessons.pattern: I will call a taxi for you.
lessons.task: I will ___ a taxi for you.
lessons.example: I will call a taxi for you.
context: Sam and Anna hail a taxi in Rome.
We hail a taxi in the street.
dialogue: Anna, we need a taxi. Where is the taxi rank?
At the end of the street. We can hail a taxi there.
Look! A moped is on the flyover.
Yes. I will call a taxi for you. The driver will give us a lift.
Good. Will the driver take us home?
Yes. The taxi will take us home at night.
lessons.listening: On Friday night, Sam and Anna need a taxi in Rome. Anna says, 'We can hail a taxi at the taxi rank.' Sam says, 'Look! A moped is on the flyover.' Anna says, 'I will call a taxi for you. The driver will give us a lift.' Sam says, 'Good.'
lessons.question: Where do Sam and Anna hail a taxi?
lessons.reading: On Friday night, Sam and Anna need a taxi in Rome. They walk to the end of the street. Anna says, 'We can hail a taxi at the taxi rank.' Sam says, 'Look! A moped is on the flyover. The city is very good at night.' Anna says, 'I will call a taxi for you. The driver will give us a lift to our hotel.' A taxi stops. The driver is a friend. He says, 'A taxi driver will give someone a lift home.' Sam says, 'Thank you. The taxi will take us home.' Anna is very happy today. She says, 'A taxi is the best way home at night.'
lessons.readingQ: Who gives Sam and Anna a lift home?
lessons.readingA: The taxi driver gives them a lift home.
lessons.speaking: Tell a friend about a taxi ride. Where do you hail a taxi? Where does it take you?
lessons.speakingSample: I hail a taxi at the taxi rank. The driver will give me a lift home. A moped is on the flyover. The city is very good at night. The driver is a friend. He says, 'I will give you a lift home.' The taxi will take me home. A taxi is the best way home at night.
lessons.writing: Write a short email to a friend about a taxi ride. Say where you hail the taxi.
lessons.writingSample: Dear Lisa, I want to tell you about a taxi ride in Rome. We hail a taxi at the taxi rank. A moped is on the flyover. The city is very good at night. The driver will give us a lift to our hotel. The driver is a friend. He says, 'I will give you a lift home.' The taxi will take us home. A taxi is the best way home at night. Best, Anna
lessons.sound: Flyover has its strongest beat on FLY. In flyover, say FLY clearly at the start. In moped, say MOPE clearly at the start.
lessons.wordTask: Where do Sam and Anna hail a taxi?
lessons.wordSample: They hail a taxi at the taxi rank.

mainWord.definition: The bar you hold on a bike.

lessons.mainWordForms: Handlebar is a noun. A handlebar is the bar you hold on a bike. Hold the handlebar with two hands.
lessons.expression: I go by bike to school.
lessons.use: Use this when you ride a bike to a place.
lessons.expressionTask: Anna rides a bike in Rome. Where does she ride?
lessons.grammar: comparatives: Cycling is faster than walking
context: Anna rides a bike in Rome.
I go by bike to school.
dialogue: Anna, do you go by bike to school?
Yes. I ride in the bike lane. It is safe.
Do you walk on the footpath too?
Yes. I walk to the park, and I ride my bike to school.
Is cycling faster than walking?
Yes. Cycling is faster than walking. Hold the handlebar with two hands.
lessons.listening: On Saturday, Anna rides a bike in Rome. She says, 'I go by bike to school. I ride in the bike lane.' Sam asks, 'Do you walk on the footpath too?' Anna says, 'Yes. I walk to the park. Cycling is faster than walking. Hold the handlebar with two hands.'
lessons.question: Where does Anna ride her bike?
lessons.reading: On Saturday, Anna rides a bike in Rome. She says, 'I go by bike to school. I ride in the bike lane. It is safe.' Sam asks, 'Do you walk on the footpath too?' Anna says, 'Yes. I walk to the park, and I ride my bike to school. Cycling is faster than walking.' Sam says, 'Hold the handlebar with two hands. Sit on the saddle.' Anna is happy. She says, 'I like to go by bike. The bike lane is good. I walk on the footpath, and I ride my bike on the road.' Sam says, 'Good. Cycling is faster than walking.' Anna smiles. She says, 'The bike is good for the city.'
lessons.readingQ: Why does Anna like to go by bike?
lessons.readingA: The bike lane is good, and cycling is faster than walking.
lessons.speaking: Tell a friend about cycling or walking. Do you go by bike? Where do you ride?

newItems.definition: Petrol or diesel for a car.

newItems.definition: A truck that moves a car that cannot move.

Do we need a tow truck?

Yes. The car needs fuel. We are late for work.

lessons.question: What is the problem with Tom's car?

lessons.speaking: Tell a friend about a car problem. What is wrong? What do you do?

He wants us to move. I will pull over and stop.

Yes. He will drop us off at the station. I can use transport English.

lessons.wordTask: Where does the driver drop Emma and Lily off?
lessons.wordSample: The driver drops them off at the station.

transferCheck.source: On Tuesday, Emma visits her teacher, Ms. Green. Emma says, 'I can use transport English in a new situation. I drive with my friend Lily to the station.' Ms. Green says, 'Good. What do you say in the car?' Emma says, 'I say, "Fasten your seatbelt, please."' Ms. Green says, 'Very good. The driver drops you off at the station?' Emma says, 'Yes. He drops us off at the station.' Ms. Green says, 'Good. You use transport English well.'
transferCheck.dictation: The driver drops Emma off at the station.
